title: Ghost and Asset
premise: Jude Coldharbour, a financial-crimes investigator who once worked deep cover, receives a calendar invite from their dead handler, Mara Voss, summoning them to a meeting that is already underway. There they discover Voss faked her death to expose Meridian Trust, the bank Jude has spent two years quietly laundering for, and that an 'accident'—a rigged gas main collapse timed to destroy evidence and witnesses—is scheduled before dawn. Hunted by both the bank's fixers and the agency that burned them, Jude must choose between the extraction flight that guarantees survival and the truth that guarantees nothing. They stay, stop the attack at the cost of their clean identity, and walk out at dawn as no one at all.
about_author: Noor Nystrom is a former compliance analyst who traded spreadsheets for suspense after a decade tracing money across three continents. They write thrillers about people whose paperwork is better than their alibis, from a coastal town where the fog never quite lifts.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. In their meticulous apartment, Jude launders a routine audit while eyeing a packed go-bag—a life built on exits. Then a calendar ping: a meeting tomorrow, 11 p.m., sent by Mara Voss, their handler, dead eleven months. The emotional beat is dread sharpening into compulsion; Jude, who trusts patterns more than people, recognizes this one as either a trap or a resurrection—and goes anyway.

chapters.title: Dead Hand
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. At the derelict ferry terminal, Jude finds not Mara but her ghost protocol: a burner phone playing her voice, laying out Meridian Trust's ledger of sins—including Jude's own signatures. A live feed shows the meeting already in progress upstairs. Emotional beat: vertigo. The person who taught Jude to survive has posthumously conscripted them, and the exit door locks behind them with a soft electronic click.

chapters.title: The Meeting
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. Hidden above, Jude watches Meridian's fixer, Ansel Roque, brief four insiders on 'the Harrow event'—an accident scheduled for 4 a.m. that will erase a whistleblower, a server room, and anyone inconvenient. Among the faces: Jude's own supervisor. Emotional beat: cold recognition. Jude films everything, then realizes the feed was bait—Mara wanted a witness inside the room, and now the room knows someone is watching.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. Fleeing through the docks, Jude calls the only number that matters—their old agency handler, Deacon—who answers with chilling calm: 'We know. Come in.' But the safe house Deacon names is already under surveillance. Emotional beat: betrayal layered on betrayal; the institutions Jude served are all reading from Meridian's script. Jude burns their own legend, scattering identities like chaff, and keeps moving.

chapters.title: What Mara Left
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. Following Mara's dead-drop chain through a laundromat and a chapel, Jude recovers her real file: proof she faked her death when the agency sold her out, plus the Harrow schematics—a gas main rigged beneath the records annex, timed to the extraction flight's departure. Emotional beat: grief curdling into resolve. Mara didn't just leave clues; she left a choice, and Jude understands they were always meant to make it alone.

chapters.title: Roque
chapters.summary: POV: Ansel Roque. The fixer's chapter: efficient, courteous, utterly hollow, Roque cleans up loose ends and interviews Jude's neighbors with wine-country charm. He identifies the go-bag's absence as confirmation Jude is active. Emotional beat: quiet menace. Through his eyes we see Jude not as hero but as asset—an item on an inventory—and learn Roque has orders to let the plane leave without him, letting the accident do the work.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. Jude tracks the Harrow target—Priya Anand, a junior auditor who found the same ledger and doesn't know she's scheduled to die. Convincing her means confessing his own crimes, trading his last clean lie for her trust. Emotional beat: reluctant intimacy. Two strangers bound by forged numbers plan sabotage together in a motel room, while outside, Roque's team tightens a perimeter Jude can feel but not yet see.

chapters.title: Four Hours to Dawn
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. Split-screen tension: Jude and Priya infiltrate the annex to disarm the rig while Deacon offers Jude a final deal—board the plane, testify sanitized, be reborn. The clock, the gas, the guards, the temptation of survival all converge. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into clarity. Jude realizes the attack isn't just destruction—it's the story Meridian will tell, and stories are the only thing Jude has ever been able to forge or break.

chapters.title: Harrow
chapters.summary: POV: Jude and alternating Roque. Climax: the rig is tripped early; in flooding corridors and failing light, Jude diverts the blast into a flooded service tunnel, sacrificing the evidence to save the people. Roque corners them, and Jude defeats him not with force but with his own recorded confession, broadcast to every phone in the building. Emotional beat: ferocious cost—Priya is wounded, the proof is gone, and dawn is arriving whether anyone deserves it or not.

chapters.title: No Fixed Address
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. Resolution: the plane leaves without them; Deacon disavows, Meridian's officers fall to Priya's surviving testimony, and Mara's grave gets a visitor who owes her everything. Jude, officially nonexistent, unpacks the go-bag for the first time in years—not to repack it, but to decide who stays. Emotional beat: hard-won peace. Identity, they finally understand, was never the alias or the badge; it's what you refuse to trade.
